result.topic_en: Ramanujan states, first assuming the prime number theorem and then the Riemann hypothesis and its analogue for ζ_2(s), the maximum order of $\overline{Q}_2(N)$ (from his work on highly composite numbers / sums of two squares), with explicit error terms and numerical constants.
result.transcription:
Add MS a 94 $^{18(36)}$ (36) (72)
(288) $2^{\log N\left\{\frac{1}{\log\log N}+O\frac{1}{(\log\log N)^2}\right\}}$.
Assuming the prime number theorem we can show that the maximum order of $\overline{Q}_2(N)$ is
(289) $2^{\frac{1}{2}Li(2\log N)+O\{\log N e^{-a\sqrt{(\log N)}}\}}$.
56. We shall now assume the Riemann hypothesis and its analogue for the function $\zeta_2(s)$. Then we can show that
(290) $2\pi_2(x)=Li\{2\vartheta_2(x)\}-2R_2(x)+O\left\{\frac{\sqrt{x}}{(\log x)^3}\right\}$,
where $R_2(x)=\frac{1}{(\log x)^2}\left\{2\sqrt{x}+\frac{1}{2}\sum\frac{x^\rho}{\rho}+\frac{1}{2}\sum\frac{x^{\rho_2}}{\rho_2}\right\}$,
where $\rho_2$ is a complex root of $\zeta_2(s)$. It can also be shown that
(291) $\sum\frac{1}{\rho}+\sum\frac{1}{\rho_2}=1+\gamma+\frac{1}{2}\log 3+3\log\frac{\Gamma(\frac{2}{3})}{\Gamma(\frac{1}{3})}$;
and so
(292) $\left\{3+\gamma+\frac{1}{2}\log 3+3\log\frac{\Gamma(\frac{2}{3})}{\Gamma(\frac{1}{3})}\right\}\sqrt{x}\geqslant R_2(x)(\log x)^2\geqslant\left\{1-\gamma-\frac{1}{2}\log 3-3\log\frac{\Gamma(\frac{2}{3})}{\Gamma(\frac{1}{3})}\right\}\sqrt{x}$
It can easily be verified that
(293) $\begin{cases}3+\gamma+\frac{1}{2}\log 3+3\log\frac{\Gamma(\frac{2}{3})}{\Gamma(\frac{1}{3})}=2.080,\\ 1-\gamma-\frac{1}{2}\log 3-3\log\frac{\Gamma(\frac{2}{3})}{\Gamma(\frac{1}{3})}=1.920,\end{cases}$
approximately. Then we can show that the maximum order of $\overline{Q}_2(N)$ is
(294) $2^{\frac{1}{2}Li(2\log N)+\phi(N)}$,
where $\phi(N)=\frac{\log(3/2)}{2\log 2}Li\left\{\frac{3}{2}(\log N)^{\frac{\log(3/2)}{\log 2}}\right\}-\frac{3(\log N)^{\frac{\log(3/2)}{\log 2}}}{4\log(2\log N)}$
$-R_2(\log N)+O\left\{\frac{\sqrt{(\log N)}}{(\log\log N)^3}\right\}$.
